mainTopic: Who passes on חלל status, how a woman becomes a חללה, and counting a כהן's punishments for forbidden women
overview: The משנה sets out which daughters may marry a כהן. A male חלל passes his disqualification to his daughters forever, but a female חללה does not. The תנאים then argue about converts and freed slaves: רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יוסי each take a different position. The גמרא explains that 'forever' means the rule never ends, unlike the three-generation limit for מצרי and אדומי. רבי יוחנן learns from the word 'בעמיו' that only males pass on the status, and the גמרא works out what happens to the daughter, the son's daughter, and the daughter's daughter. The גמרא also shows that רבי דוסתאי disagrees with the משנה. A ברייתא proves that the woman herself becomes a חללה through a forbidden relationship with a כהן, and another ברייתא defines a חללה as one born from a פסול כהונה. Finally, a ברייתא counts how many punishments a כהן receives when a woman carries several forbidden statuses, and the גמרא begins to ask what case 'widow, widow, widow' describes.

steps.title: A male חלל's daughter is unfit forever
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens: the daughter of a male חלל may never marry a כהן, no matter how many generations pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: The daughter of a male חלל is unfit to marry into the כהונה forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states its first rule: a male חלל passes his disqualification to his daughters, and it never wears off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל is the son of a כהן from a marriage the Torah forbids to a כהן. His daughters, and the daughters of his male descendants, count as חללות. The word 'forever' is what the גמרא will ask about later.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
A son of a כהן from a forbidden marriage; he loses the status of כהונה
Unfit or disqualified
The priesthood; here, being able to marry a כהן
Forever

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The daughter of a male chalal
phrases.notes: A חלל is the son of a כהן and a woman a כהן may not marry.

phrases.english: is unfit for the priesthood forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת חָלָל זָכָר פְּסוּלָה מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה לְעוֹלָם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter of a male חלל is permanently unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: Only the father's חלל status passes to the daughter
steps.stepSummary: If the mother is a חללה and the father a regular Jew, the daughter is fit. If the father is a חלל, the daughter is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A regular Jew who married a חללה: his daughter is fit for the כהונה. A חלל who married a regular Jewish woman: his daughter is unfit for the כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares two cases to show that only the father passes on חלל status, not the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases mirror each other. When the חלל parent is the mother, the daughter is fit. When the חלל parent is the father, she is unfit. The גמרא will later ask for the source of the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman with חלל status
Fit or permitted
A regular Jewish woman (not a כהן's family and not a convert)

steps.whyThisMatters: This mirror pair is the base for the גמרא's question 'מנא הני מילי' later in this section.

phrases.english: An Israelite who married a chalala:
his daughter is fit for the priesthood.
A chalal who married a Jewish woman:
his daughter is unfit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּשָׂא חֲלָלָה בִּתּוֹ כְּשֵׁירָה לַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies that the rule of step 1 depends on the father, not the mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter gets חלל status only from her father, not from her mother.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a male גר is like a male חלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the daughter of a male גר is unfit for the כהונה, just like the daughter of a male חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The daughter of a male גר is like the daughter of a male חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה takes the rule about a male חלל and applies it to a male convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a convert father disqualifies his daughter from marrying a כהן, even if her mother is born Jewish. This opens the debate about converts that the next תנאים continue.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
Like the daughter of

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר.
phrases.english: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male chalal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of the male חלל to a male גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the daughter of a male גר is unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only two convert parents disqualify
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says a daughter is fit if even one parent is born Jewish. Only a daughter of two converts is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: A regular Jew who married a convert woman, his daughter is fit for the כהונה. A convert who married a Jewish woman, his daughter is fit for the כהונה. But a convert who married a convert woman, his daughter is unfit for the כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with רבי יהודה and lists three cases of converts marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against רבי יהודה, a convert father alone does not disqualify, as long as the mother is born Jewish. A convert mother with a Jewish father is also fine. Only when both parents are converts is the daughter unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: A female convert
But; marks the one case that is different

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not say a convert is like a חלל. He disqualifies only the daughter of two converts, so a born-Jewish parent on either side makes her fit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
An Israelite who married a female convert:
his daughter is fit for the priesthood;
and a convert who married a Jewish woman:
his daughter is fit for the priesthood;
but a convert who married a female convert:
his daughter is unfit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּשָׂא גִּיּוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי יהודה about a male גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter is unfit for the כהונה only if both of her parents are converts.

steps.title: Converts and freed slaves: the rule lasts until a Jewish-born mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that converts and freed slaves are the same, and the disqualification continues even for ten generations, until a mother is born Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both converts and freed slaves are the same, even up to ten generations, until the girl's mother is from a born-Jewish family.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב continues his ruling and explains how long the disqualification lasts and who else it includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freed עבדים כנענים are treated like converts. If convert families keep marrying convert families, the daughters stay unfit even after many generations. Once a born-Jewish woman becomes a mother in the line, her daughter is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Freed non-Jewish slaves, who become full Jews when freed
Generations
Until the mother is born Jewish

phrases.english: Both a convert and freed slaves are the same,
even up to ten generations,
until his mother is from Israel.
phrases.notes: 'His mother' means the mother of the child in that generation. Once she is born Jewish, the line becomes fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד גֵּר וְאֶחָד עֲבָדִים מְשׁוּחְרָרִים אֲפִילּוּ עַד עֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule to freed slaves and to later generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children of convert or freed-slave lines stay unfit, even for ten generations, until a born-Jewish mother enters the line.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: even a daughter of two converts is fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי is the most lenient. Even the daughter of a convert who married a convert may marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even a convert who married a convert woman, his daughter is fit for the כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and permits even the case that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (even) shows that רבי יוסי agrees with the earlier lenient cases and goes further. For him, convert status does not disqualify a daughter from the כהונה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Even; adds a further, stronger case

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on converts. רבי יהודה says a male גר disqualifies. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only two convert parents disqualify. רבי יוסי says converts never disqualify.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even a convert who married a female convert:
his daughter is fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אַף גֵּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא גִּיּוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about the daughter of two converts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the daughter of two converts is fit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'forever'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word 'לעולם' in the משנה comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is meant by 'forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed the extra word 'forever'. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word looks unnecessary, because a disqualification normally lasts unless we are told otherwise. The גמרא wants to know what wrong idea this word blocks.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is 'forever'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'לעולם' adds to the rule about a חלל's daughter.

steps.title: Not like the Egyptian and Edomite, whose limit ends after three generations
steps.stepSummary: The word 'forever' teaches that the חלל rule is not like מצרי and אדומי, whose restriction ends after three generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it is just like an Egyptian and an Edomite: just as there it ends after three generations, so too here it ends after three generations. So the משנה teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'forever' blocks a mistaken comparison to the Egyptian and Edomite convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An Egyptian or Edomite convert's children may marry into the community from the third generation. Someone might think the חלל disqualification ends the same way. 'Forever' tells us it never ends.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; brings up a mistaken idea
Just like; compares to another case
Egyptian and Edomite converts, limited for three generations
It teaches us; the wrong idea is rejected

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is just like an Egyptian and an Edomite,
phrases.notes: דברים 23:8-9

phrases.english: just as there it is after three generations,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן נָמֵי לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: so too here, also after three generations;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא מִידֵּי דַּהֲוָה אַמִּצְרִי וַאֲדוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Forever' rules out comparing the חלל to מצרי ואדומי, whose restriction ends after three generations.
steps.whatToRemember: The חלל disqualification never ends, unlike מצרי ואדומי.

steps.title: What is the source that a חללה mother does not disqualify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a Jew who married a חללה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An Israelite who married a חללה.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source showing that a חללה mother does not make her daughter unfit. The next step brings the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only the father passes on חלל status. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that females do not pass it on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? A request for a source

phrases.english: 'An Israelite who married a chalala.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה from step 2.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a חללה mother does not disqualify her daughter.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'among his people' means males, not females
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'בעמיו' in two פסוקים. Just as a כהן's impurity laws apply to males only, so only males pass on חלל status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון: It says here, 'And he shall not profane his offspring among his people,' and it says there, 'He shall not make himself impure, a chief man among his people.' Just as there it is males and not females, so too here it is males and not females.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question with a גזירה שוה, linking two פסוקים that share the word 'בעמיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a כהן becoming impure from a dead body applies only to male כהנים. Since both פסוקים say 'בעמיו', the profaning of offspring is also limited to males. So a male חלל disqualifies his children, but a חללה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
It says here, and it says there; the form of a גזירה שוה
Among his people; the shared word that links the פסוקים
Males and not females

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the Torah basis for the משנה's rule that חלל status passes only through the father.
steps.whatToRemember: Only a male חלל passes on the disqualification, learned through 'בעמיו' from the impurity laws of כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
It is stated here:
"And he shall not profane his offspring among his people,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

phrases.english: and it is stated there:
"He shall not make himself impure, a chief man among his people."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:4

phrases.english: Just as there it is males and not females,
phrases.notes: The ban on a כהן becoming impure applies to male כהנים, not their daughters.

phrases.english: so too here it is males and not females.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נֶאֱמַר כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'בעמיו' shows that only males profane their offspring, so a חללה mother does not disqualify her daughter.

steps.title: Then the כהן גדול's daughter should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: If only males pass on חלל status, the daughter of a כהן גדול who married a widow should be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, the daughter of a כהן גדול should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the males-only rule from the previous step. If only males are affected, a daughter born from a forbidden marriage should not become a חללה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה said only males are affected, just like a כהן's טומאה laws. Taken literally, that would mean only a son becomes a חלל and a daughter never does. That clashes with the well-known law that such a daughter is a חללה.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (a formula that pushes an idea to an uncomfortable result)
High Priest, who may not marry a widow
She should be permitted

phrases.english: But if that is so,
the daughter of a High Priest should be permitted!
phrases.notes: He means a כהן גדול who married a widow, a marriage the Torah forbids him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the males-only גזירה שוה from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The males-only rule learned from בעמיו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only males are affected, the daughter of a forbidden priestly marriage should never become a חללה

steps.title: The verse says 'offspring,' which includes a daughter
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says זרעו, his offspring, not 'his son,' so the daughter is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'his son'? It is written 'his offspring': 'He shall not profane his offspring among his people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק uses a word that covers both sons and daughters. So the daughter is a חללה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זרעו covers all children, so the daughter of the כהן גדול is clearly unfit. The males-only rule still matters one generation later: the daughter of that חללה is fit. The next steps work out exactly where the line falls.

keyTerms.meaning: His offspring (sons and daughters)
Is it written? (pointing to the exact wording of a פסוק)
He shall not profane

phrases.english: Is it written 'his son'?
'His offspring' is written,
'He shall not profane his offspring among his people.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by pointing to the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The males-only rule would exempt the daughter herself
steps.terutzMaskana: The daughter is included through זרעו; the males-only rule applies only from the next generation on

steps.title: Then the son's daughter should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only covers direct offspring, the granddaughter through his son should be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of his son should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes one generation further. The פסוק speaks of 'his offspring,' meaning his own children, so the next generation should be outside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זרעו clearly covers the כהן גדול's own children. His grandchildren are not obviously included. So the question is why the son's daughter should be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: His son's daughter

phrases.english: The daughter of his son should be permitted!
phrases.notes: The פסוק only clearly covers his own children, so the next generation seems to fall outside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 12 to challenge the next generation
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading זרעו as covering only direct children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only direct offspring are included, a grandchild through the son should be fit

steps.title: The offspring is compared to the father
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares the offspring to the כהן גדול himself. Just as his daughter is unfit, so is his son's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'He shall not profane his offspring,' comparing his offspring to him. Just as his daughter is unfit, so too his son's daughter is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a comparison drawn from the פסוק. The son, who is a חלל, is treated like his father, so his daughter is unfit too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase links the offspring to the father, a היקש. The חלל son acts like a new 'father' whose daughter is unfit. This explains why a male חלל keeps passing on the status.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a היקש, linking two things in the פסוק)
Unfit (to marry a כהן)

phrases.english: It is written: 'He shall not profane his offspring,'
comparing his offspring to him:
just as he, his daughter is unfit,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן גדול who married a widow.

phrases.english: so too his son, his daughter is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son's daughter is outside the verse and fit
steps.terutzMaskana: The son is treated like the father, so his daughter is unfit

steps.title: Then the daughter's daughter should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Using the same comparison, the daughter of the חללה should also be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of his daughter should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the comparison around. If the offspring is just like the father, the חללה daughter should also pass on the status to her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש made the son act like his father. Nothing in the comparison itself limits it to sons. So it seems the daughter's daughter should be unfit as well.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter's daughter
She should be forbidden

phrases.english: The daughter of his daughter should be forbidden!
phrases.notes: His חללה daughter married a regular Jew. The same comparison seems to make her daughter unfit too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the היקש of step 14 to the daughter's line
steps.kashyaTarget: The היקש comparing offspring to father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every offspring is like the father, a daughter should also pass on the status

steps.title: Otherwise the גזירה שוה would teach nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the daughter's daughter were unfit, the males-only גזירה שוה would have no purpose. So she is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the גזירה שוה accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גזירה שוה must teach something. What it teaches is that a female חללה does not pass the status on to her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש and the גזירה שוה each cover their own area. The היקש makes sons pass on the status, and the גזירה שוה stops it from passing through daughters. So the daughter's daughter is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another through a shared word in two פסוקים
What does it accomplish?

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's daughter: unfit (זרעו). His son's daughter: unfit (היקש). His daughter's daughter: fit (גזירה שוה). The status only passes through males.

phrases.english: If so,
what does the verbal analogy accomplish for him?
phrases.notes: This is the בעמיו comparison from step 10, which taught that only males pass on the status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מַאי אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by showing the גזירה שוה would otherwise be useless
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source must have a purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughter's daughter is unfit through the היקש
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה makes the daughter's daughter fit

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat the case of a male חלל?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's case of a חלל who married a Jewish woman seems already covered by its opening line.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A חלל who married a Jewish woman, his daughter is unfit.' But the first clause already taught: 'The daughter of a male חלל is unfit for the priesthood forever'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה and asks why it is needed. The opening line already said a male חלל's daughter is unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening clause stated the general rule about a male חלל. The later clause gives a specific case with the same result. It looks like the משנה is repeating itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
But it already taught this!
A man disqualified from כהונה because of a forbidden priestly marriage

phrases.english: A חלל who married a Jewish woman:
his daughter is unfit.
But it already taught this in the first clause:
'The daughter of a male חלל
is unfit for the priesthood forever'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The later clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later clause repeats what the first clause already said

steps.title: The משנה wanted a matching pair
steps.stepSummary: Because the משנה taught a Jew who married a חללה, it also taught the reverse case for balance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught in the first clause a Jew who married a חללה, it also taught in the last clause a חלל who married a Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה lists both cases side by side to make a complete pair. The second case is there for balance, not for a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a Jew who married a חללה does teach something new: her daughter is fit. Once the משנה taught that case, it set out the opposite case beside it so the picture is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (it taught one thing, it taught the other)
The last clause of the משנה
A woman disqualified from marrying a כהן

phrases.english: Since it taught in the first clause
a Jew who married a חללה,
it also taught in the last clause
a חלל who married a Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause is a pointless repeat
steps.terutzMaskana: It was included only to match the earlier case

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה holds that marrying a regular Jew 'cleans' the line from either side, so even a male חלל's daughter would be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, as it was taught: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says, just as Jewish men are a purifying מקוה for חללות, so Jewish women are a purifying מקוה for חללים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה does not follow a ברייתא with a different opinion. רבי דוסתאי says the children are fit whenever one parent is a regular Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a male חלל who marries a Jewish woman has an unfit daughter. רבי דוסתאי disagrees: just as a regular Jewish husband 'cleans' a חללה's line, a regular Jewish wife 'cleans' a חלל's line.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is not in line with (a certain opinion)
A purifying מקוה (here, a picture of 'cleaning' the family line)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says:
Just as Jewish men
are a purifying ritual bath for חללות,
phrases.notes: A חללה who marries a regular Jew has fit daughters. The husband 'cleans' the line.

phrases.english: so too Jewish women
are a purifying ritual bath for חללים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes a dissenting view on the clause just discussed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי דוסתאי, a regular Jewish parent of either gender makes the children fit

steps.title: What is רבי דוסתאי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי דוסתאי's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי דוסתאי son of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי דוסתאי gets his view. This sets up the next step, which gives his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His view goes against the plain flow of our משנה, so the גמרא wants to see his textual basis.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason
of רבי דוסתאי son of רבי יהודה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי דוסתאי's view

steps.title: Profaning only happens within 'one people'
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי reads בעמיו as 'with his own kind': the child is a חלל only when both parents are חללים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'He shall not profane his offspring among his people.' He profanes with one people, but with two peoples he does not profane.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי דוסתאי's source. He reads the word בעמיו as limiting the status to a child whose parents are both חללים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used the word בעמיו for a males-only rule. רבי דוסתאי reads the same word differently: if one parent is a regular Jew, the parents are 'two peoples,' and the child is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says
Among his people
Peoples (here, two different family statuses)
Profanes (makes a חלל)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה: a male חלל passes on the status even when he marries a regular Jew. רבי דוסתאי: a regular Jewish parent of either gender 'cleans' the line, based on בעמיו.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'He shall not profane his offspring among his people':
it is with one people that he profanes,
phrases.notes: Read בעמיו as 'with his own kind': the child is a חלל only when both parents are חללים.

phrases.english: with two peoples he does not profane.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ בְּעַמָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בעמיו means the status passes only when both parents are of the same flawed status

steps.title: The child is covered, but what about the woman herself?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that 'לא יחלל זרעו' teaches only that the child is a חלל, and asks for the source that the woman also becomes a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'He shall not profane his offspring.' This tells me only about his offspring. How do I know that she herself is also profaned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that asks for a source. The פסוק talks about the child, so how do we know the woman also becomes a חללה? This sets up the proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the פסוק mention only 'זרעו', his offspring. The woman's status is not stated, so the ברייתא wants a separate source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
He shall not profane his offspring
A woman disqualified from marrying a כהן
From where do we know?

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"He shall not profane his offspring"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

phrases.english: I have only his offspring;
she herself, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: 'She' is the woman the כהן was forbidden to be with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אין לי אלא זרעו, היא עצמה, מנין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the source for the woman's own status as a חללה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the woman herself becomes a חללה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the child to the woman
steps.stepSummary: If the innocent child becomes a חלל, then surely the woman who sinned becomes a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it is a קל וחומר: if his offspring, who did not sin, is profaned, isn't it logical that she, who did sin, is profaned?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers its first proof, a קל וחומר. The child did nothing wrong and is still disqualified, so the woman, who did do wrong, should surely be disqualified too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic runs from the weaker case to the stronger one. Having no sin did not protect the child, so having a sin should certainly bring disqualification to the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Committed a sin
Becomes profaned (gets the status of a חלל)
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: You can say: it is a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: מָה זַרְעוֹ שֶׁלֹּא עָבַר עֲבֵירָה – מִתְחַלֵּל,
phrases.english: if his offspring, who did not commit a sin, is profaned,
then she, who did commit a sin,
isn't it logical that she is profaned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That the woman herself becomes a חללה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the child, who becomes a חלל even though he did not sin.

steps.title: The כהן himself sinned and is not disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is challenged: the כהן also sinned, yet he does not become a חלל, so sinning does not automatically lead to disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself will prove otherwise: he committed a sin, and he is not profaned!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks the קל וחומר by pointing to the כהן himself. He sinned too, but he does not become a חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that sinning makes you more likely to be disqualified. The כהן shows a case where someone sinned and was not disqualified, so that assumption seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (otherwise); used to break a קל וחומר with a counterexample

phrases.english: He himself will prove otherwise,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן who had the forbidden relationship.

phrases.english: since he committed a sin and is not profaned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from the child to the woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן sinned and is not disqualified, which shows that sinning does not make someone a חלל.

steps.title: A man is never disqualified this way, but a woman can be
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected: a male כהן never becomes a חלל through a forbidden relationship, while a woman can lose her fitness, so the כהן is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about him? He is never profaned in any case. Can you say the same about her, who can be profaned in every case?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the challenge. The כהן is a man, and a man never becomes a חלל, so his case says nothing about a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can lose her fitness to marry a כהן in many situations, but a man never loses his status this way. Because the two cases are so different, the counterexample does not work and the קל וחומר survives.

keyTerms.meaning: What about this case? It has a special feature (used to show two cases are not alike)
In every case

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהוּא, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין מִתְחַלֵּל בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: What about him? He is not profaned in any case;
will you say the same about her, who can be profaned in every case?

steps.triggerLanguage: מה להוא, שכן אין מתחלל בכל מקום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the קל וחומר by showing that the counterexample in step 24 does not apply.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a man is never disqualified, but a woman can be.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's case shows that sinning does not cause disqualification.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן is not a fair comparison, so the קל וחומר still stands.

steps.title: A backup proof from the wording of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Even if the קל וחומר is rejected, the פסוק itself hints at the woman: 'יחלל' can be read as 'shall not become profaned', which fits someone who was fit and then lost that status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish to say the reasoning fails, the verse says: 'He shall not profane his offspring.' Read it as 'shall not become profaned', which describes someone who was fit and then became profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second proof in case the קל וחומר does not hold. It reads the word in the פסוק as describing someone who was once fit and then became disqualified, and that is the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child was never fit to begin with, so 'becoming profaned' cannot really describe him. Only the woman, who was fit before the forbidden relationship, can 'become' profaned, so the פסוק is pointing to her.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish to say (the first proof fails); introduces a backup proof
The verse says
Was fit and then became profaned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. 'יְחַלֵּל' means 'he will profane', but the ברייתא reads it as 'יְחוּלַּל', 'will become profaned', and that reading only fits someone who was fit before.

phrases.english: And if you wish to say that this reasoning fails:
the verse says, "He shall not profane his offspring":
read it as 'shall not become profaned',
phrases.notes: The same letters are being read as 'become profaned' instead of 'he will profane'.

phrases.english: meaning this one, who was fit and then became profaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם נפשך לומר: אמר קרא לא יחלל זרעו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a backup proof in case the קל וחומר fails.
steps.raayaObject: That the woman herself becomes a חללה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading 'לא יחלל' as 'לא יחולל', which describes someone who was fit and then became profaned.

steps.title: What was wrong with the קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what weakness the phrase 'ואם נפשך לומר' is referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'if you wish to say' that the reasoning fails?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a backup proof at all. What problem with the קל וחומר was it worried about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 already defended the קל וחומר against the כהן's case. So the backup proof must be answering a different problem, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (the meaning of)?

phrases.english: What is meant by "if you wish to say"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the phrase that introduced the backup proof in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness in the קל וחומר the phrase 'אם נפשך לומר' is pointing to.

steps.title: The child was made through a sin, so the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר could be refuted because the child was created through a sin and the woman was not, so the ברייתא falls back on the reading 'לא יחולל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say there is a way to refute it: what about his offspring? He was formed through a sin. Then the verse says 'He shall not profane', read as 'shall not become profaned', meaning one who was fit and then became profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the weakness. The child was created through a forbidden act, which the woman was not, so you cannot learn her law from his. That is why the reading of the פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר treated the child as the weaker case, but the child has a special flaw: his very creation came through a sin. Because of that flaw, the comparison breaks down, and the woman's status has to come straight from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say
There is a way to refute (the argument)
His creation came about through a sin

steps.whatToRemember: The woman who had a forbidden relationship with a כהן becomes a חללה herself. The קל וחומר from the child can be refuted, because the child was formed through a sin. So the firm source is the פסוק, read as 'לא יחולל': someone who was fit and then became profaned.

phrases.english: And if you would say there is a way to refute it:
what about his offspring? He was formed through a sin;
then the verse says: "He shall not profane":
read it as 'shall not become profaned':
meaning this one, who was fit and then became profaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי תימא איכא למיפרך: מה לזרעו שכן יצירתו בעבירה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by identifying the weakness in the קל וחומר, which explains why the פסוק is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קל וחומר can be refuted because the child was formed through a sin, so the source for the woman's status is the reading 'לא יחולל'.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines a חללה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a חללה is any woman born from 'the disqualified ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Who is a חללה? Any woman born from the disqualified ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that gives a short definition of a חללה. The next steps will try to figure out what 'disqualified ones' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties חללה status to birth: she comes from 'disqualified' parents. It does not say whom the parents are disqualified for, and that gap drives the next several steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman disqualified from marrying a כהן
Disqualified people
The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Who is a חללה?
Any woman who was born from the disqualified ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that defines חללה, after the earlier talk about how a woman can become one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חללה is any woman born from the disqualified ones.

steps.title: What does 'disqualified' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'disqualified ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'disqualified ones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'disqualified ones' refers to. This question sets up the next move, where it tries one possible meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is unclear. It could mean people forbidden to each other, or people unfit for כהונה. The גמרא needs to pin it down.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (meant by)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'disqualified ones'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what a word in the ברייתא means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom the 'disqualified ones' are disqualified for.

steps.title: 'Forbidden to him' cannot be the meaning
steps.stepSummary: If 'disqualified' meant a woman forbidden to that man, the case of remarrying a divorcée disproves it, because her children are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means disqualified for him, that cannot be. A man who remarries his divorcée is with a woman forbidden to him, yet her children are fit. The verse says 'it is an abomination': she is the abomination, but her children are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one meaning, 'forbidden to him,' and knocks it down using the case of a man who remarries his divorcée.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remarrying one's divorcée, after she married someone else in between, is forbidden. Still, the פסוק 'תועבה היא' teaches that only she is the abomination and the children are not. So being born from a forbidden couple does not by itself make a child a חללה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
One who remarries his divorced wife
Abomination
Fit, not disqualified

phrases.english: If you say it means disqualified for him,
but there is one who remarries his divorcée,
phrases.notes: This is a divorcée who married someone else in between, so going back to her is forbidden.

phrases.english: who is forbidden to him, and yet her children are fit,
as it is written: 'it is an abomination' —
phrases.notes: דברים 24:4

phrases.english: she is an abomination, but her children are not abominations!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא פְּסוּלִים לוֹ, הֲרֵי מַחֲזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Children born from a man and the divorcée he remarried come from a forbidden couple, yet the פסוק says they are fit.

steps.title: רב יהודה: disqualified for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the ברייתא means a woman born from someone disqualified for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what it means. Who is a חללה? Any woman born from someone disqualified for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new reading. 'Disqualified' means disqualified for כהונה, not just forbidden to that man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids the divorcée problem. The remarried divorcée is forbidden to her husband, but that does not damage כהונה status. The ברייתא is only talking about relationships that are a כהונה problem, like a כהן with a woman forbidden to כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone disqualified with respect to כהונה
This is what it means

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This is what it is saying:
Who is a חללה?
Any woman born from someone disqualified for כהונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 30 with a reading that avoids the problem in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the ברייתא

steps.title: A woman can become a חללה without being born one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא suggests only birth makes a חללה, yet a widow, divorcée or זונה can become one later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that only a woman born this way is a חללה, and one not born this way is not? But a widow, a divorcée or a זונה was not born that way, and yet she becomes a חללה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's reading. The phrase 'born from' sounds like the only way to be a חללה, but we know other ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording suggests that being born from a פסול כהונה is the only path to becoming a חללה. But women such as a widow with a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or זונה with a כהן, become חללות through that forbidden relationship. This ties back to steps 22 to 28. So the definition seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Born, yes; not born, no (an inference from the wording)
Widow
Divorcée
A woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: Born, yes; not born, no?
But there is a widow, a divorcée, a זונה,
phrases.notes: These women become חללות when they are with a כהן who is forbidden to them, as learned back in steps 22 to 28.

phrases.english: who were not born that way, and yet she becomes a חללה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading that a חללה is one born from a פסול כהונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording suggests birth is the only way, but women can become חללות later through a forbidden relationship.

steps.title: רבה: the ברייתא means the חללה who was never fit
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ברייתא is only describing the חללה who never had a moment of fitness, meaning the one born from a פסול כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is what it means. Which mentioned חללה never had any moment of fitness at all? Any woman born from someone disqualified for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the objection by narrowing the ברייתא's question. It is not listing every חללה, only the kind who was disqualified from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow, divorcée or זונה was fit before and lost her status. The ברייתא is asking about a חללה who was never fit at all, and only a woman born from a פסול כהונה fits that. The word 'מוזכרת' (mentioned) in רבה's version raises a new question.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of fitness
Mentioned
At all

phrases.english: Rabba said:
This is what it is saying:
Which is the mentioned חללה

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר כְּלָל?
phrases.english: who never had a moment of fitness at all?
Any woman born from someone disqualified for כהונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 33 by limiting what the ברייתא is asking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא defines every type of חללה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא defines only the חללה who was never fit at all.

steps.title: What does 'mentioned' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבה meant by the word 'mentioned.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'mentioned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the word 'מוזכרת' in רבה's version: mentioned where? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה called her 'the mentioned חללה,' but he did not say where she is mentioned. The גמרא wants that explained.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'mentioned'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in רבה's answer.

steps.title: 'Mentioned' means written openly in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבין explains that 'mentioned' means the חללה whose status comes straight from the Torah and needs no explanation from the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rav Yitzchak bar Avin said: This is what it means. Which חללה has her basis in the words of the Torah, so that we do not need to explain her from the words of the Sages? Any woman born from those disqualified for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבין explains 'mentioned' as written plainly in the Torah, which describes the daughter born from a פסול כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child born from a פסול כהונה is stated openly in the Torah. A woman who becomes a חללה through a forbidden relationship is learned only through the Sages' reading 'לא יחולל' (step 26). So the ברייתא is asking about the חללה the Torah states openly.

keyTerms.meaning: Her basis is in the words of the Torah
The words of the Sages, meaning their reading of the פסוק
To explain

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's חללה 'born from a פסול כהונה' is the one stated openly in the Torah, who was never fit. Women who lose their fitness also become חללות, but that is learned through the Sages' reading of the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דברי סופרים' here does not mean a rabbinic law. It means the Sages' reading of the פסוק, and the result is still Torah law.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avin said:
This is what it is saying:
Which is the חללה
whose basis is from the words of the Torah
and we do not need to explain her from the words of the Sages?
phrases.notes: He means the woman who becomes a חללה through a forbidden relationship, learned from the Sages' reading 'לא יחולל.'

phrases.english: Any woman born from those disqualified for כהונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'mentioned.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Mentioned' means stated openly in the Torah, unlike the חללה learned through the Sages' reading of the פסוק.

steps.title: Repeated 'widow' or 'divorcée' brings only one liability
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that 'widow, widow, widow' brings only one liability, and so does 'divorcée, divorcée, divorcée.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Widow, widow, widow, he is liable only once. Divorcée, divorcée, divorcée, he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about punishment. When the same prohibition, widow or divorcée, is repeated, there is only one liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the same label three times does not create three separate prohibitions. Since it is the same prohibition each time, he gets only one punishment. The ברייתא does not yet explain the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to punishment
He is liable only once

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A widow, a widow, a widow:
he is liable only once.
A divorcée, a divorcée, a divorcée:
he is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how many punishments a כהן receives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating the same prohibition (widow or divorcée) brings only one liability.

steps.title: The order of her statuses decides how many liabilities
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. When a woman became an אלמנה, גרושה, חללה, and זונה in that order, the כהן גדול is liable for each. In the reverse order, he is liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was a widow, then a divorcée, then a חללה, then a זונה, in that order, he is liable for each one. If she first became a זונה, then a חללה, then was divorced, then widowed, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It adds a case where one woman has four different forbidden statuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one woman carries several statuses at once, not just one status repeated. The ברייתא teaches that the order in which she got them changes the result. In order, he gets a separate liability for each. In reverse order, he gets only one. The ברייתא does not give the reason yet. It only states the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In order. Here it means widow first, then divorcée, then חללה, then זונה.
Liable for each and every one, meaning a separate punishment for each status
She became a זונה
She became a חללה
She became a widow

steps.confusionAlert: This is one woman with four statuses, not four different women. The only difference between the two cases is the order in which her statuses came.

phrases.english: A widow, and a divorcée, and a חללה, a זונה,
phrases.notes: This is all one woman who picked up each status, one after another.

phrases.english: when they are in order,
he is liable for each and every one.
If she became a זונה and became a חללה,
and was divorced and was widowed,
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה וּגְרוּשָׁה וַחֲלָלָה זוֹנָה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם כַּסֵּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא begun in step 37, moving from one repeated status to several different statuses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Statuses gained in the order widow, divorcée, חללה, זונה each bring a separate liability. In reverse order, there is only one liability.

steps.title: What case is 'widow, widow, widow'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line 'widow, widow, widow – only one liability' again and asks what situation it describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: widow, widow, widow – he is liable for only one. What kind of widow case is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא to study it. It asks what case 'widow, widow, widow' is talking about. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the word 'widow' three times but never says what situation it means. Before the rule can be understood, the גמרא needs to pin down the case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' The גמרא uses this to quote a line from a source it is about to analyze.
'What are the circumstances?' A request to define the case

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 37.

phrases.english: widow, widow, widow,
he is liable for only one.
This widow, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא has been fully quoted, the גמרא returns to its first clause to define the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case does the ברייתא mean by 'widow, widow, widow'?

steps.title: Three different men's widows should mean three liabilities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is three widows of three different men. It then challenges this: why would that bring only one liability?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he was with the widow of ראובן, the widow of שמעון, and the widow of לוי, why is he liable for only one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning, three separate widows, and immediately shows that it doesn't fit the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three different women means three separate forbidden acts, so we would expect three liabilities. Since the ברייתא says only one, this reading seems wrong. The גמרא will need a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say.' This introduces a suggested reading that is about to be challenged.
The widow of ראובן. Here ראובן, שמעון, and לוי are just sample names for three different men.
Why?

phrases.english: If we say that he had relations with the widow of ראובן,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אַלְמְנַת שִׁמְעוֹן וְעַל אַלְמְנַת לֵוִי,
phrases.english: and with the widow of שמעון, and with the widow of לוי,
why is he liable for only one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question of step 39 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'widow, widow, widow' means three widows of three different men
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three separate women are three separate forbidden acts. That should bring three liabilities, not the single liability the ברייתא states.
